intro: Xenia is our service area's second county seat — founded in 1803 at the forks of the Shawnee creeks, named from the Greek for hospitality. It is the only town in our service area hit by two violent tornadoes: the F5 of April 3, 1974 and the F4 of September 20, 2000 on nearly the same track — then rebuilt both times (80% of destroyed homes rebuilt within a year of the F5, everything by 1984). Its housing is 1970s-heavy: 23.0% built in that single decade, 71.4% pre-1980. The 1886 Shawnee Creek flash flood killed 28.
